Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
23-year-old female with worsening, constant lower abdominal pain for a few days, associated light vaginal spotting and nausea.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant lower-mid abdominal pain x “few days,” worsening, 8/10 severity.  
• Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding since period ended 2 weeks ago; mild vaginal discharge; nausea without vomiting; constipation last week (resolved); no fever, dyspnea, shoulder pain, urinary pain/frequency, syncope.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not documented).  
• Medications/contraception: Etonogestrel implant placed ~1 year ago; others not documented.  
• OB/GYN: Last menstrual period ≈2 weeks ago; cycles irregular on implant; negative pregnancy test 1 month ago; no previous pregnancies.  
• Social: School teacher; lives with husband & in-laws; denies recreational drugs; smoking and alcohol intake unclear (patient responded “I don’t know”); travel abroad 1 year ago.  
• Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
• No in-person exam performed during video consult.  
• Vitals: Not obtained.

Impression:
Worsening lower abdominal pain of uncertain etiology; differential includes gynecological causes—rule out pregnancy.

Plan:
• Arrange urgent face-to-face clinic visit for abdominal and pelvic examination—patient to phone support line to book.  
• Perform urine pregnancy test today; instructed to call back immediately if positive.  
• Safety-net advice: Present sooner if pain markedly worsens, unable to keep fluids down, or other concerning symptoms develop.  
• No medications prescribed pending assessment.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: vitals, physical exam findings, full medication list, detailed allergy reaction, alcohol/smoking status clarification, review of systems beyond discussed items.  
● Internal conflicts: Unclear response regarding alcohol/smoking (“I don’t know”).  
● Transcript quality: Several inaudible/unfinished statements; personal identifiers omitted.
